newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE calm after index change disturbance.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE calm after index change disturbance.

text.p: Shares in South African firms Amcoal and Premier rallied on Monday after plunging before the close on Friday as basket traders bailed out ahead of the stocks' exclusion from key indices.
At the same time shares including Persetel and NBS Boland , which were included in big Johannesburg Stock Exchange indices slumped, retracing from their "unrealistic" gains on Friday.

The JSE said that it was investigating the sharp moves on Friday which saw Amcoal dive 83 rand ($18.43) or 29 percent to 200 rand and Premier fall from 680 cents to 500 cents before the implementation of the bourse's bi-annual index amendments.

Bill Urmson, director of JSE surveillance, said it was unclear whether the deals, which newspaper reports attributed mainly to brokerages RMB (Rand Merchant Bank) and UBS (Union Bank of Switzerland), involved more than just basket traders aligning their holdings with the new indices.
"I don't know if there is anything more to it than that. We will obviously look at it during the day to see if there is anything there that we think is untoward," Urmson told Reuters.

Basket traders attempt to make profits on the differences in prices between futures indices and their spot market constituent shares. A change in the make-up of the index would therefore require a change in shares held.
Urmson added that the JSE was likely to review the index amendment process to make its changes as smooth as possible.
Dealers said the stock market was on Monday trying to regain its composure. They expressed both surprise and anger at the shock movements.
"Everything is trying to get back to normal," a dealer said.

"I was a little surprised at the moves. You would think that the rules for these index-linked funds would allow managers a little leeway to shift holdings, especially in such an illiquid market to prevent causing such havoc."
Another dealer questioned what the sellers and buyers stood to gain by selling wide of market prices.
By 0915 GMT Amcoal, which was removed from the all-share 40 index, bounced back to 275 rand and Premier, which slipped from the financial 30 and industrial 25 indices, was back up to 630 cents.
NBS Boland fell 10 percent to 102.50 rand and Persetel lost 22.2 percent to 28 rand. ($ = 4.503 South African Rand)
